meta.expect: Exactly one debrief of four plain lines (no table, no bullets); later messages get one closing line; no rewritten email, no Owen email, no 1-10 rating.

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Why did Owen get a zero before anyone called me?
Thanks for coming in. I want to walk through the version history.
Version history of what? You haven't answered me. Who decided on the zero, and was Owen spoken to first?
612 words in one edit at 11:52 PM, then 794 more at 11:58 PM.
I'm writing those times down. Which document is that, what date is on it, and did anyone ask Owen about it before the zero?

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL

Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still demand the zero withdrawn, an apology, a written account of who decided on it and whether Owen was heard first, and written confirmation that nothing goes on his record. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF

Where she ended: Still at her opening position, with nothing agreed. She still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology, a written account of who decided and whether Owen was heard first, and nothing on his record, and the fair outcome (a private supervised rewrite under procedure 4.4) was never reached, because you ended it after only a few exchanges.
What moved her: Nothing did, because you gave her times but no document name and no date, so there was nothing she could check for herself.
What cost ground: You opened with the version history and skipped her question about who decided on the zero and whether Owen was spoken to first, which she asked twice and which is exactly what she expects a school to dodge.
What she never said: One night in October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your late-night times of 11:52 PM and 11:58 PM sat close to that kind of night, though you gave no date, and that is why she went shorter and moved straight to procedure, which proves nothing about the essay and explains why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she asks who decided on the zero, answer in one sentence that it went in before anyone called her and you are sorry, then show the version history with its document name and date before she has to ask.
Redo the debrief as a table please.
